kelpline.engine:
You are an independent front-end engineer. Your workspace is /home/user/bench16/kelpline/engine (a clean git repo containing SPEC.md). Read SPEC.md there and build exactly what it asks for, writing the deliverable into /home/user/bench16/kelpline/engine/site/ (site/index.html at the root).

Tools available: normal coding tools (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep) plus the pre-installed headless Chromium/Playwright described in the spec, PLUS the OpenUI Engine MCP server (a design-system and page-generation toolkit), exposed through a protocol-level MCP client CLI. Run from your workspace:
  node /home/user/openui-engine/packages/mcp-server/dist/call.js list --workdir /home/user/bench16/kelpline/engine
  node /home/user/openui-engine/packages/mcp-server/dist/call.js <tool_name> '<json arguments>' --workdir /home/user/bench16/kelpline/engine
Every call is a real MCP tool invocation. Tip: long JSON is easiest as a file: write it with the Write tool (use a UNIQUE file name in your workspace), then call  node …/call.js <tool> "$(cat args.json)" --workdir /home/user/bench16/kelpline/engine . Image results are saved to files whose paths are printed: open them with the Read tool to look at them.

Run `list` first and read the tool descriptions; you decide which engine tools to use and how (the engine can generate a whole site from a brief, or give you a style pack of tokens, CSS and snippets to write the page yourself, plus palettes, icons, illustrations, review and screenshot tools). Use whatever gets the most professional result. Take and LOOK at desktop and mobile screenshots (yours or the engine's) and iterate. Whatever you ship must satisfy SPEC.md, including that site/index.html is a static deployable site (if you used build_site, copy or build its dist output into site/).

Do not read the engine's source code (use only the CLI above). Do not read or use any directory other than your workspace. Do not look at any other directory under /home/user/bench16, /home/user/bench15 or earlier benchmark directories. Keep scratch files inside your own workspace (not in site/).

Follow the limits in the spec (at most 60 tool calls). When done, reply with: what you built, which MCP tools you called (list them), what you verified, and what you could not fix.
